job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his grandfather, Mr. Sharma, were walking through their lush garden in Dehradun on 12th May. Rohan noticed a tall banyan tree and asked how it stays hydrated. Mr. Sharma explained that plants have a special internal system, much like our own blood vessels, to move water from the roots to the leaves. He pointed to a small stream nearby, noting that water flows downhill because of gravity. 'Just as the stream needs a path to move, the tree uses tiny tubes called xylem to transport water upward,' he said. Rohan then saw a butterfly resting on a flower. Mr. Sharma mentioned that animals have a heart to pump blood throughout their bodies, ensuring oxygen reaches every cell. Because the heart beats continuously, blood circulates to keep the animal active. Rohan felt tired after their 2-hour walk and sat on a bench. He realized that both the giant tree and the tiny butterfly rely on these internal transport systems to survive. Mr. Sharma smiled, happy that his grandson understood the importance of these hidden networks in nature.
response.summary: Rohan learns about how plants and animals transport essential substances within their bodies. He compares the movement of water in trees to the circulation of blood in animals.
